# AI speak patterns, part 3

Built from the packs in `hooks/lib/patterns`. Each section names its own source.

The category index is in `ai-speak-patterns.md`.

## undue-emphasis

Presets: `ryan`, `all`. Source: Pangram signs-of-ai-writing frequency counts and Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch.

Intensifiers, stacked qualifiers, or markup used to manufacture stress.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `extremely`, `remarkably`, `utterly`, `undeniably`, `unquestionably`, `exceptionally`, `tremendously`, `immensely` | cut |
| a stress word in bold or italics | remove the bold, state the fact |
| a stress word in capitals mid-sentence | use normal case |
| Intensifiers, stacked qualifiers, or markup used to manufacture stress. | `minPairs = 2` |

very, highly, deeply, and particularly report only when two of them share a sentence. A line-initial admonition label with a colon stays unflagged.

## vague-attribution

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch, Wikipedia:Weasel word, Simple Wikipedia avoid-weasel-words.

A claim attributed to an unnamed authority.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `experts say`, `experts agree`, `experts argue`, `experts believe` | name the expert |
| `studies show`, `studies suggest`, `studies indicate` | cite the study |
| `research has shown`, `research shows`, `research suggests` | cite the source |
| `it is widely believed`, `it is widely known`, `it is widely accepted`, `it is widely held` | name who believes it |
| `many argue`, `many believe`, `many say`, `many feel` | name who |
| `some observers argue`, `some observers say`, `some observers note`, `some observers suggest`, `some analysts argue`, `some analysts say`, `some analysts note`, `some analysts suggest` | name the observer |
| `industry reports suggest`, `industry reports indicate`, `industry reports say`, `industry observers suggest`, `industry observers indicate`, `industry observers say` | cite the report |
| `it has been said that`, `it has been reported that`, `it has been observed that`, `it is said that`, `it is reported that`, `it is observed that` | name the source |
| `critics argue`, `critics say`, `critics contend` | name the critic |
| `sources say`, `sources indicate`, `sources suggest` | name the source |

A correctly sourced sentence is flagged the same as an unsourced one: the pattern cannot see a citation that follows.

## vocabulary

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Words that appear far more often in model output than in human writing.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `delve`, `delves`, `delved`, `delving` | look at, examine |
| `tapestry` | describe the actual parts |
| `realm` | area, field |
| `embark`, `embarks`, `embarked`, `embarking` | start |
| `beacon` | rewrite |
| `testament to` | shows, proves |
| `robust` | reliable, or the measured property |
| `comprehensive` | complete, full |
| `cutting-edge` | latest, or name the version |
| `leverage`, `leverages`, `leveraged`, `leveraging` (verb) | use |
| `pivotal` | important, or say what depends on it |
| `meticulous`, `meticulously` | careful |
| `seamless`, `seamlessly` | works without X, name X |
| `nestled` | is in, sits |
| `vibrant` | describe what is active |
| `thriving` | growing, or cite a number |
| `showcases`, `showcasing` (verb) | shows |
| `deep dive` | look at, examine |
| `dive into` | look at |
| `bustling` | busy |
| `intricate`, `intricacies` | complex, or name the complexity |
| `ever-evolving` | changing |
| `daunting` | hard |
| `holistic`, `holistically` | complete, or list what is included |
| `actionable` | practical, or drop |
| `impactful` | effective, or name the effect |
| `learnings` | lessons, findings |
| `thought leader`, `thought leadership` | expert, or name the work |
| `best practices` | what works, the standard approach |
| `synergy`, `synergies` | describe the combined effect |
| `interplay` | relationship |
| `symphony` (as metaphor) | describe the coordination |
| `state-of-the-art` | name the benchmark |
| `world-class`, `best-in-class` | cite a comparison |
| `future-proof` | say what changes it survives |
| `empower`, `empowers`, `empowered`, `empowering` | let, enable |
| `crucial` | important, or say what breaks without it |
| `incredibly` | cut |
| `competitive edge` | name the advantage |
| `vast experience` | years and scope |
| `excited to announce` | state the fact |
| `humbled` | cut |
| `paradigm` | model, approach |
| `load-bearing`, `load bearing` (as metaphor) | essential, or say what breaks without it |
| `underscores the`, `underscored how`, `underscore that`, `underscores why` | shows |
| `the landscape`, `today's landscape`, `current landscape`, `evolving landscape`, `competitive landscape`, `digital landscape`, `tech landscape`, `business landscape`, `AI landscape`, `landscape of` | field, market, or cut |

| Flagged (tier 2) | Fix |
|---|---|
| `harness`, `harnesses`, `harnessed`, `harnessing` | use |
| `navigate`, `navigates`, `navigating` | handle, or name the work |
| `foster`, `fosters`, `fostering` | build, cause |
| `elevate`, `elevates`, `elevated` | improve, raise |
| `unleash`, `unleashes`, `unleashed`, `unleashing` | release, start |
| `streamline`, `streamlines`, `streamlined` | simplify, speed up |
| `bolster`, `bolsters`, `bolstered`, `bolstering` | strengthen, add to |
| `spearhead`, `spearheads`, `spearheaded`, `spearheading` | lead |
| `resonate with`, `resonates with` | matches, appeals to |
| `facilitate`, `facilitates`, `facilitated` | help, run |
| `underpin`, `underpins`, `underpinning` | supports |
| `nuanced` | name the difference |
| `multifaceted` | list the parts |
| `ecosystem` | the tools, the parts |
| `myriad`, `plethora` | many, or the number |
| `encompass`, `encompasses`, `encompassed` | includes, covers |
| `catalyze`, `catalyzes`, `catalyzed`, `catalyst for` | causes |
| `reimagine`, `reimagines`, `reimagined` | redesign |
| `galvanize`, `galvanizes`, `galvanized` | prompt, spur |
| `augment`, `augments`, `augmented`, `augmenting` | add to |
| `cultivate`, `cultivates`, `cultivated` | build, grow |
| `illuminate`, `illuminates` | shows, explains |
| `elucidate`, `elucidates` | explain |
| `juxtapose`, `juxtaposes`, `juxtaposed` | compare |
| `cornerstone` | the main part |
| `paramount` | most important |
| `poised to` | about to, or say when |
| `burgeoning` | growing |
| `nascent` | new, early |
| `quintessential` | typical |
| `overarching` | main, general |
| `transformative` | describe the change |

Tier-2 verbs and nouns report only when two or more of them share a paragraph, so a single ordinary use stays quiet. `load-bearing` before a structural noun (`wall`, `beam`, `column`, `joist`, `truss`, `member`, `footing`, `slab`, `stud`, `partition`, `masonry`, `lintel`, `pier`, `rafter`, `girder`, `capacity`), with up to one adjective in between, is building terminology and stays unflagged. `bearing down`, `bearing on`, and `bearing upon` are the literal verb and stay unflagged.

## word-frequency

Presets: `statistical`, `all`.

Flags text that leans on one favorite word far more than natural word spread predicts.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags text that leans on one favorite word far more than natural word spread predicts. | `minWords = 200`, `maxShare = 0.035` |

Share of the text taken by its most repeated content word. The research's Zipf exponent is unreachable at this text size, so the share replaces it.

## wordiness

Presets: `ryan`, `ste`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Long forms of short words.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `utilize`, `utilise`, `utilizes`, `utilized`, `utilizing`, `utilising` | use |
| `in order to` | to |
| `due to the fact that` | because |
| `commence`, `commences`, `commenced` | start |
| `ascertain` | find out |
| `endeavor`, `endeavors`, `endeavored`, `endeavoring`, `endeavour`, `endeavours`, `endeavoured`, `endeavouring` | try, effort |
| `prior to` | before |
| `subsequent to` | after |
| `in the event that` | if |
| `at this time`, `at this point in time` | now |
| `for the purpose of` | to, for |
| `with regard to` | about |
| `in conjunction with` | with |
| `in accordance with` | as in, follow |
| `is capable of`, `are capable of`, `has the ability to`, `have the ability to` | can |
| `a number of` | some, or the number |
| `a large number of` | many, or the number |
| `it is necessary to` | you must |
| `in the vicinity of`, `in close proximity` | near |
| `the majority of` | most |
| `in spite of the fact that` | although |

A hit here is a writing fix and says nothing about who wrote the text.

## ai-attribution

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `minimal`, `git`, `all`. Source: Group G research: claude-code#1296, Codex CLI commit attribution, VS Code #314311, Cursor forum #168258, docs.devin.ai.

A commit or PR trailer credits an AI tool as co-author, generator, or signer.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Generated with [Claude Code]` | drop the generated-with line |
| `Generated with Devin` | drop the generated-with line |
| `Made with Cursor` | drop the made-with line |
| a `Generated-By:` trailer | drop the trailer |
| `This commit was generated by` | drop the disclosure sentence |
| an `Assisted-by:` trailer | drop the trailer |
| `Signed-off-by:` plus a `[bot]` account | drop the bot sign-off |
| `Signed-off-by:` plus an AI tool email | drop the bot sign-off |

| Flagged (tier 2) | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Co-authored-by:` plus an AI tool name | drop the co-author trailer |
| `Co-authored-by:` plus an AI tool email | drop the co-author trailer |

The two `Co-authored-by` patterns sit at tier 2. A trailer that pairs an AI tool name with an AI email reports; a co-author named Claude with a personal address stays quiet.

## ai-identity

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `minimal`, `git`, `all`. Source: Group G research: claude-code#72477, VS Code #314311, Cursor forum #168258, gemini-cli #11447.

The commit author or committer field names an AI tool instead of a person.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `--author=` naming an AI tool | use a human author name |
| `--author=` holding an AI tool email | use a human email address |
| `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` set to an AI tool | use a human author name |
| `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` set to an AI tool | use a human committer name |
| `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` on an AI tool domain | use a human email address |
| `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` on an AI tool domain | use a human email address |
| `git config user.name` or `user.email` set to an AI tool | set a human name or email |
| a numeric-id GitHub bot address | use a human email address |

| Flagged (tier 2) | Fix |
|---|---|
| `--author=` naming a bare AI tool name | use a human author name |
| `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` or `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` set to a bare AI tool name | use a human author name |

Bare first names such as `Claude`, `Devin`, and `Gemini` sit at tier 2, so a person who sets their own identity with a personal email produces one hit and stays quiet. A repo that commits as a bot on purpose lists `ai-identity` in `excludePacks`.

## ai-tool-mention

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `git`, `all`. Source: Group G research: anthropics/claude-code#1296 and anthropics/claude-code#66602.

Names of AI coding tools, or the agent narrating its own process instead of the change.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `as requested by the user` | state the change directly |
| `per the user's instructions` | state the change directly |
| `per the assistant`, `per the model`, `per the AI` | state the change directly |
| `as suggested by the assistant`, `as suggested by the model`, `as suggested by the AI` | state the change directly |
| `the model suggested`, `the assistant wrote` | state the change directly |
| `AI-generated`, `AI generated` | cut the disclosure |
| `with AI assistance` | cut the disclosure |
| `generated by AI`, `written by an AI` | cut the disclosure |
| `generated by` or `written with` a named AI tool | cut the tool name |
| a `git commit` command naming an AI tool | cut the tool name |

A tool name reports only next to process wording (`generated by`, `written by`, `suggested by`) or inside a `git commit` command, so a comment that just names a tool stays clean. That wording around `the model` or `the assistant` reports as well, which a repo whose subject is model output drops with `disablePatterns`.

## benefit-tail

Presets: `ryan`, `technical`, `git`, `all`. Source: Group G research: AI-generated PR summary and commit body conventions.

A sentence ends in a justification clause tacked on after a comma.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `, which improves readability` and the like | cut the justification clause |
| `, making it easier to maintain` | cut the justification clause |
| `, for better performance` | cut the justification clause |
| `, ensuring consistency` | cut the justification clause |
| `, so that it's more robust` | cut the justification clause |

The noun list stays abstract on purpose. A tail that names a measured effect, such as `cuts p99 latency to 90ms`, does not match.

## canned-review

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `git`, `all`. Source: Group G research: PR review boilerplate.

Stock PR-review phrasing used regardless of what the diff actually does.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `LGTM with minor nits` | cut, or approve plainly |
| `Looks good to me` | cut, or approve plainly |
| `Nice work` | cut |
| `Great work on this` | cut |
| `One small suggestion` | state the suggestion |
| `Minor nitpick` | state the point |
| `Overall, this looks good` | cut, or approve plainly |
| `solid implementation` | cut |
| `well-structured` | cut, or name the structure |
| `clean implementation` | cut |
| `It might be worth considering` | state the suggestion |

`Consider adding tests` and `I'd suggest` are left out. Careful reviewers open with them before a concrete point, which held the full list under 85% precision.
